items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k Applied to a Polynomial
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f = f.sum fun i r => (Polynomial.monomial (i - k)) (↑(i.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $ and a polynomial $ f \in R[X] $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ applied to $ f $ is given by $ D^{(k)}(f) = \sum_{i} \binom{i}{k} \cdot a_i \cdot X^{i - k} $, where $ a_i $ is the coefficient of $ X^i $ in $ f $. This expression sums over all monomials in $ f $, scaling each by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{i}{k} $ and reducing the exponent by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Order k on Polynomial Ring
items.type: {R : Type u_1} → [inst : Semiring R] → ℕ → Polynomial R →ₗ[R] Polynomial R
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the Hasse derivative of order $ k $ is an $ R $-linear map $ D^{(k)} : R[X] 	o R[X] $ defined by $ D^{(k)}(a_i X^i) =  inom{i}{k} a_i X^{i - k} $ on monomials and extended linearly. This operation generalizes the usual derivative by scaling each coefficient $ a_i $ by the binomial coefficient $  inom{i}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Product Rule for Hasse Derivatives in Polynomial Rings
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f g : Polynomial R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) (f * g) =
    ∑ ij ∈ Finset.antidiagonal k, (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.1) f * (Polynomial.hasseDeriv ij.2) g
items.informal_description: For any polynomials $ f, g \in R[X] $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the product $ f \cdot g $ satisfies $$ D^{(k)}(f \cdot g) = \sum_{\substack{i + j = k}} D^{(i)}(f) \cdot D^{(j)}(g), $$ where the sum is taken over all pairs $ (i, j) $ of natural numbers such that $ i + j = k $. This expresses the Hasse derivative of a product as a sum over the antidiagonal decomposition of $ k $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient Formula for Hasse Derivative of Order k
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) f).coeff n = ↑((n + k).choose k) * f.coeff (n + k)
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of a polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $ is equal to $ \binom{n + k}{k} $ multiplied by the coefficient of $ X^{n + k} $ in $ f $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative of Monomial in Polynomial Ring
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k n : ℕ) (r : R),
  (Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) ((Polynomial.monomial n) r) = (Polynomial.monomial (n - k)) (↑(n.choose k) * r)
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative of the monomial $ rX^n $ in the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ is given by $ \binom{n}{k} r X^{n - k} $. This expresses how the Hasse derivative acts on monomials by scaling the coefficient by the binomial coefficient $ \binom{n}{k} $ and reducing the degree by $ k $.

items.informal_name: Hilbert Polynomial Successor Formula
items.type:
∀ {F : Type u_1} [inst : Field F] (p : Polynomial F) (d : ℕ),
  p.hilbertPoly (d + 1) = ∑ i ∈ p.support, p.coeff i • Polynomial.preHilbertPoly F d i
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ p $ over a field $ F $ and natural number $ d $, the Hilbert polynomial of $ p $ at $ d + 1 $ is equal to the sum over the support of $ p $ of the product of the coefficient of $ p $ at exponent $ i $ and the pre-Hilbert polynomial of degree $ d $ evaluated at $ i $. Formally, $ \text{hilbertPoly}(p, d + 1) = \sum_{i \in \text{support}(p)} (\text{coeff}_i(p)) \cdot \text{preHilbertPoly}_F(d, i) $.

items.informal_name: Hasse Derivative Composition Formula with Binomial Coefficient
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k l : ℕ),
  Polynomial.hasseDeriv k ∘ₗ Polynomial.hasseDeriv l = (k + l).choose k • Polynomial.hasseDeriv (k + l)
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $ and natural numbers $ k, l $, the composition of the $ k $-th and $ l $-th Hasse derivatives on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $ equals $ \binom{k + l}{k} $ times the $ (k + l) $-th Hasse derivative, i.e., $ D^{(k)} \circ D^{(l)} = \binom{k + l}{k} D^{(k + l)} $.

items.informal_name: Factorial Scaling of Hasse Derivative Equals Iterated Derivative
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (k : ℕ), ⇑(k.factorial • Polynomial.hasseDeriv k) = (⇑Polynomial.derivative)^[k]
items.informal_description: For any semiring $ R $, the $ k $-th Hasse derivative operator on the polynomial ring $ R[X] $, when multiplied by $ k! $, equals the $ k $-th iterate of the standard derivative operator. Formally, $ k! \cdot D^{(k)} = (\frac{d}{dX})^k $, where $ D^{(k)} $ denotes the Hasse derivative of order $ k $.

items.informal_name: Coefficient of Taylor Expansion at $ r $: $ \text{coeff}_n(f(X + r)) = D^{(n)}f(r) $
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_1} [inst : Semiring R] (r : R) (f : Polynomial R) (n : ℕ),
  ((Polynomial.taylor r) f).coeff n = Polynomial.eval r ((Polynomial.hasseDeriv n) f)
items.informal_description: For any polynomial $ f $ over a semiring $ R $, natural number $ n $, and element $ r \in R $, the coefficient of $ X^n $ in the Taylor expansion $ f(X + r) $ equals the evaluation of the $ n $-th Hasse derivative of $ f $ at $ r $. The Hasse derivative $ D^{(n)} $ scales monomials $ a_i X^i $ by $ \binom{i}{n} a_i X^{i - n} $.

      "informal_name": "Linear Equivalence Between Family of Linear Maps and Linear Maps on Finite Support Functions",

items.informal_name: Linear Equivalence Between Family of Linear Maps and Linear Maps on Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N) (l : α →₀ M), ((Finsupp.lsum S) f) l = l.sum fun b => ⇑(f b)
items.informal_description: The linear equivalence $\text{Finsupp.lsum}$ establishes a bijection between families of $\sigma$-linear maps $\alpha \to M \to_\sigma N$ and $\sigma$-linear maps on finite support functions $\alpha \to_0 M \to_\sigma N$. For a family $F$, the forward direction maps a finite support function $d$ to the sum $\sum_{i \in \text{support } d} F(i)(d(i))$, while the inverse direction composes a linear map $F$ with the single-index embedding $\text{lsingle}_i$. The equivalence is proven by verifying additivity, scalar multiplication compatibility, and bijectivity via $\text{lsingle}$ composition.

items.informal_name: Linear Combination of Vectors Indexed by α over R
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} (R : Type u_5) [inst : Semiring R] [inst_1 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_2 : Module R M]
  {v : α → M} (l : α →₀ R), (Finsupp.linearCombination R v) l = l.sum fun i a => a • v i
items.informal_description: The linear map from the space of finite support functions $ \alpha \to_0 R $ to the module $ M $, which sends each finite support function $ l $ to the sum $ \sum_{i \in \text{support } l} l(i) \cdot v_i $, where $ v_i $ denotes the vector associated with index $ i $. This map is constructed using the linear equivalence of summing scalar multiples of individual vectors embedded via the right scalar multiplication operation.

items.informal_name: Application of Finitely Supported Sum of Linear Maps
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_4} {R₂ : Type u_5} {M : Type u_6} {M₂ : Type u_7} {ι : Type u_8} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M₂] {σ₁₂ : R →+* R₂} [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : Module R₂ M₂] {γ : Type u_9} [inst_6 : Zero γ] (t : ι →₀ γ) (g : ι → γ → M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) (b : M),
  (t.sum g) b = t.sum fun i d => (g i d) b
items.informal_description: For semirings $ R $ and $ S $ with a ring homomorphism $ \sigma: R \to S $, an $ R $-module $ M $, and an $ S $-module $ M_2 $, given a finite support function $ t: \iota \to \gamma $ and a function $ g: \iota \to \gamma \to M \to M_2 $ producing $ \sigma $-linear maps, the application of the finitely supported sum $ \sum_{t} g(i, d) $ to a vector $ b \in M $ equals the sum over $ t $'s support of $ g(i, d)(b) $. Formally, $ (\sum_{t} g)(b) = \sum_{t} g(i, d)(b) $.

items.informal_name: Linear Equivalence Between Families of Linear Maps and Linear Maps on Finite Support Functions
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {M : Type u_2} {N : Type u_3} {R : Type u_5} {R₂ : Type u_6} (S : Type u_8) [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : Semiring S] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : AddCommMonoid N] [inst_6 : Module R₂ N] {σ : R →+* R₂} [inst_7 : Module S N] [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R₂ S N]
  (f : α → M →ₛₗ[σ] N), ⇑((Finsupp.lsum S) f) = fun d => d.sum fun i => ⇑(f i)
items.informal_description: The linear equivalence $\text{Finsupp.lsum}$ establishes a bijection between families of $\sigma$-linear maps $\alpha \to M \to_\sigma N$ and $\sigma$-linear maps on finite support functions $\alpha \to_0 M \to_\sigma N$. For a family $F$, the forward direction maps a finite support function $d$ to the sum $\sum_{i \in \text{support } d} F(i)(d(i))$, while the inverse direction composes a linear map $F$ with the single-index embedding $\text{lsingle}_i$. This equivalence preserves additivity and scalar multiplication compatibility.

items.informal_name: Evaluation of a finitely supported sum of linear maps
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_4} {R₂ : Type u_5} {M : Type u_6} {M₂ : Type u_7} {ι : Type u_8} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M₂] {σ₁₂ : R →+* R₂} [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : Module R₂ M₂] {γ : Type u_9} [inst_6 : Zero γ] (t : ι →₀ γ) (g : ι → γ → M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂),
  ⇑(t.sum g) = ⇑(t.sum fun i d => g i d)
items.informal_description:
Let $t: \iota \to_0 \gamma$ be a function with finite support, and let $g$ be a function that maps a pair $(i, d) \in \iota \times \gamma$ to a semilinear map $g(i, d): M \to M_2$. The theorem states that the coercion from linear maps to functions commutes with this sum. In other words, for any element $x$ in the domain module $M$, the action of the sum of the linear maps on $x$ is the sum of the actions of each linear map on $x$:
$$ \left(\sum_{i \in \text{supp}(t)} g(i, t(i))\right)(x) = \sum_{i \in \text{supp}(t)} \left(g(i, t(i))(x)\right) $$
where $\text{supp}(t)$ is the finite support of $t$.

items.informal_name: Application of Sum of Linear Maps as Sum of Applications
items.type:
∀ {R : Type u_7} {R₂ : Type u_8} {M : Type u_9} {M₂ : Type u_10} {ι : Type u_11} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : Semiring R₂] [inst_2 : AddCommMonoid M] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid M₂] {σ₁₂ : R →+* R₂} [inst_4 : Module R M]
  [inst_5 : Module R₂ M₂] {γ : ι → Type u_12} [inst_6 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_7 : (i : ι) → Zero (γ i)]
  [inst_8 : (i : ι) → (x : γ i) → Decidable (x ≠ 0)] (t : Π₀ (i : ι), γ i) (g : (i : ι) → γ i → M →ₛₗ[σ₁₂] M₂) (b : M),
  (t.sum g) b = t.sum fun i d => (g i d) b
items.informal_description: For a dependent finite support function $ t $ and a family of linear maps $ g $, applying the sum of $ g(i, t(i)) $ to an element $ b $ is equal to the sum over the support of $ t $ of $ g(i, t(i))(b) $.

items.informal_name: Linear Map Applied to Linear Combination Distributes Over the Combination
items.informal_description: For any linear map $ f : M \to M' $ between $ R $-modules and any finite support function $ l : M \to_0 R $, applying $ f $ to the linear combination $ \sum_{m \in \text{support } l} l(m) \cdot m $ yields the linear combination $ \sum_{m \in \text{support } l} l(m) \cdot f(m) $. In symbols: $ f\left(\sum_{m} l(m) \cdot m\right) = \sum_{m} l(m) \cdot f(m) $.

items.informal_name: Application of Linear Equivalence for Dependent Finite Support Functions via Summation
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_1} {R : Type u_3} (S : Type u_4) {M : ι → Type u_5} {N : Type u_6} [inst : Semiring R]
  [inst_1 : (i : ι) → AddCommMonoid (M i)] [inst_2 : (i : ι) → Module R (M i)] [inst_3 : AddCommMonoid N]
  [inst_4 : Module R N] [inst_5 : DecidableEq ι] [inst_6 : Semiring S] [inst_7 : Module S N]
  [inst_8 : SMulCommClass R S N] (F : (i : ι) → M i →ₗ[R] N) (a : Π₀ (i : ι), M i),
  ((DFinsupp.lsum S) F) a = (DFinsupp.sumAddHom fun i => (F i).toAddMonoidHom) a
items.informal_description: For a semiring $ R $, index type $ \iota $, family of $ R $-modules $ \{M(i)\}_{i \in \iota} $, and another $ R $-module $ N $, applying the linear equivalence $ \mathrm{lsum} $ to a family of linear maps $ \{F_i : M(i) \to_R N\} $ results in a linear map $ \Phi $ such that for any dependent finite support function $ a $, $ \Phi(a) $ equals the sum over the support of $ a $ of $ F_i(a(i)) $. This equivalence is defined using component-wise summation of the images under $ F_i $.
